page: Google Cloud Platform a4-highgpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized server instance designed for heavy computational workloads. It features 224 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 3968.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 17.71 GB of RAM per core. The primary hardware acceleration is delivered via eight integrated NVIDIA B200 GPUs from the Blackwell family, offering a combined total of 1440 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

This instance family is engineered for massive parallel processing tasks where GPU-to-GPU communication and high-capacity VRAM are critical. While benchmark data is not available for this specific configuration, the hardware profile indicates a high-density resource allocation suitable for large-scale deployments. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the consolidation of eight high-tier GPUs and nearly four terabytes of system memory into a single node reduces the overhead of multi-node cluster management for workloads that fit within these resource boundaries.

The a4-highgpu-8g is optimized for demanding artificial intelligence and machine learning workloads, including large language model training, complex deep learning inference, and high-performance data science jobs. It is also highly applicable for advanced scientific simulations, molecular modeling, and large-scale parallel rendering tasks that require substantial GPU memory and dedicated CPU compute resources.
